case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
**Short answer:** I expect pier salmon fishing to be below average at all four ports this week. The data I have can't separate them, so I'm rating them nearly the same.

No DNR reports are available for this question, so none of this comes from fishing reports. It rests on one buoy summary and the general reference. The tool gave me only weekly buoy averages for the week before 2025-09-16. It returned no modeled pierhead temperatures, no cold-layer depths and no wind forecast.

**Ratings (0 slow to 4 excellent)**

| Port | Buoy surface temp (measured) | Change over the week | My rating |
|---|---|---|---|
| St. Joseph (buoy 45026) | 69 F | -1 F | 1 |
| South Haven (buoy 45168) | 69 F | -0 F | 1 |
| Grand Haven (buoy 45161) | 68 F | +1 F | 1 |
| Muskegon (buoy 45161) | 68 F | +1 F | 1 |

Grand Haven and Muskegon share the same buoy, so they get the same reading.

**Evidence**
- Surface water is 68–69 F at every port. The reference says Chinook and coho prefer 52–58 F, with an optimum of 53 F (NY DEC, general guidance). Surface water this warm is well above that range.
- Michigan Sea Grant / MSU Extension (general guidance) says mature Chinook in early fall hold in or near water of 55 F or less. They come toward pierheads mainly when a north or east wind causes upwelling, and a sharp drop in buoy temperature is the sign of one.
- None of the four buoys shows a sharp drop. The changes are -1 to +1 F, which is flat. That means no upwelling is under way.

**My read**
- I'd expect most salmon to be offshore, holding deeper where the water is cooler, and out of reach of pier anglers. Without upwelling, I'd expect only occasional fish from the piers.
- The 1 F differences between ports are too small to mean anything. Grand Haven and Muskegon are warming slightly, and St. Joseph is cooling slightly. I wouldn't lean on that.
- If you want one port, I'd pick St. Joseph. That is close to a coin flip, and it rests only on that 1 F cooling.
- A better plan is to watch the wind forecast. If a north or east wind of a day or more is coming, check the modeled pierhead temperature. A drop of several degrees at a port would make it my pick. I'd expect ratings of 2–3 in that case, but only then.

**Caveats**
- I have no information on pier closures or access.
- I have no wind forecast, so I can't say whether conditions are safe or whether upwelling is likely.
- I have no lures, depths or recent catch details, because those would have to come from reports.

**Bulletin links:** None. No DNR reports were available.
